[11] 6. The Recipient will, on request from the Discloser, return all copies and records of the Confidential Information to the Discloser and will not retain any copies or records of the Confidential Information.
[12] 7. Neither this Agreement nor the supply of any information grants the Recipient any licence, interest or right in respect of any intellectual property rights of the Discloser except the right to copy the Confidential Information solely for the Purpose.
[13] 8. The undertakings in clauses 2 and 3 will continue in force indefinitely.
[14] 9. This Agreement is governed by, and is to be construed in accordance with, English law.
[15] The English Courts will have non-exclusive jurisdiction to deal with any dispute which has arisen or may arise out of, or in connection with, this Agreement.

The document says return upon request, not upon termination. This is a weak entailment - typically in these NDA auditing tasks, "on request" return is considered entailment for return obligations. Evidence: [11]. → Entailment

The hypothesis says "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." The document grants the right to copy for the Purpose, so it does grant some right. Hmm, but the hypothesis is about not granting rights. Since the agreement explicitly grants a right to copy, this could be a contradiction. But typically "no licensing" hypotheses are entailed when the agreement says no license granted. The exception for copying doesn't contradict "no licensing" per se. Let me think: hypothesis says "Agreement shall not grant Receiving Party any right to Confidential Information." The document says no licence/interest/right is granted EXCEPT right to copy solely for Purpose. So strictly, the document grants a right, which contradicts "shall not grant any right"? The hypothesis says may share with third-parties including consultants, agents, professional advisors. Clause 3 prohibits disclosure to any third party. So Contradiction with [6].
- nda-17 (Permissible copy): Segment [12] grants right to copy solely for the Purpose. → Entailment, evidence [12].
- nda-8 (Notice on compelled disclosure): Segment [10] allows disclosure required by law but doesn't require notice. → NotMentioned.
- nda-13 (Permissible acquirement of similar information): Not mentioned. → NotMentioned
- nda-5 (Sharing with employees): Not mentioned - clause 3 prohibits third party disclosure, no employee exception. → NotMentioned
- nda-4 (Limited use): Segment [5] says not to use for any purpose except the Purpose. → Entailment, evidence [5].
